content.cause1: A genuine stock shortage at the shop
content.cause3: A delivery split across more visits than were recorded
content.disclaimer: This report states a difference and the evidence for it. It does not establish a cause and does not allege wrongdoing by any person or shop. A difference like this can have many causes, including entirely ordinary ones; establishing the cause is for the shop and the grievance process, not for this tool.
content.causeRedirect: RationSaathi can't say why a difference happened, and doesn't guess. It only shows the arithmetic and your evidence. A difference can have many causes — a stock shortage, an e-PoS or biometric failure, a delivery split across visits, or a recording error. Finding the cause is for the shop and the grievance process. If you want it looked into, you can prepare a grievance from your report and file it on the official portal.

labels.shortfallExplain: The counted quantity is less than the entitlement for this period. This tool does not know why.
labels.lateExplain: This record's date is outside the period being checked. It is still counted.
labels.unrecordedExplain: No slip, SMS, photo or note is linked to this record, so it is not counted.
labels.unclearExplain: Marked as unsure (by you, or because machine-read values were not checked), so it is not counted until confirmed.

whatIsUnrecorded.a: Unrecorded means you said you received some grain, but no slip number, SMS, photo or note is linked to it. Such records are listed in the report but not counted in the total, because there is nothing to show for them. If you find a slip or SMS later, edit the record and add it.

whatIsUnclear.a: Unclear means a record is marked as unsure: either you ticked "I'm not sure", or a value read from a photo or voice was not checked by you. Unclear records are not counted until you confirm them.

whatIsLate.a: Late means the date of a record falls outside the month you are checking — for example, October's grain collected on 3 November. The record is still counted for the month you are checking; the label only notes the date.

whatIsShortfall.a: Shortfall means the counted quantity you received is less than the entitlement under the rule you confirmed. It describes the numbers only. It does not say why the difference exists — that is for the shop and the grievance officer to look into.

afterFiling.q: What happens after I file a grievance?
afterFiling.a: The portal gives you a reference number. Save it in RationSaathi. Your grievance goes to the officials responsible for your area, who may look into it and respond. You can check its status on the official portal using the reference number. If you are not satisfied, the National Food Security Act provides for a District Grievance Redressal Officer (DGRO) and a State Food Commission.

whatIsDgro.a: DGRO stands for District Grievance Redressal Officer. Under the National Food Security Act, 2013, each district has an officer who hears grievances about entitlements under the Act. Your state food department or its helpline can tell you who the DGRO is for your district. Check the details in the channel directory, and note that entries may not be verified.

findFpsNumber.q: Where do I find my FPS (shop) number?
findFpsNumber.a: The fair price shop (FPS) number is often printed on your ration card, on the e-PoS slip you get at the shop, or in the SMS sent after distribution. Many state food department websites also let you look up your card details, including the shop it is attached to.

whatIsEntitlement.q: How much am I entitled to?
whatIsEntitlement.a: Under the national NFSA scale, Priority Household (PHH) cards get 5 kg of foodgrains per member per month, and Antyodaya (AAY) cards get 35 kg per family per month. Your state may give more under its own scheme. RationSaathi shows the national figure as a starting point and lets you change it — the calculation uses only the rule you confirm.

whyOtp.q: Why can't RationSaathi submit the grievance for me?
whyOtp.a: The official portal asks for an OTP sent to your Aadhaar-linked mobile. Only you should enter it, on the official website. RationSaathi never asks for your Aadhaar number or OTP. It prepares the text and fields so you can copy them across and submit yourself.

whatEvidence.a: Any of these: the number on the e-PoS slip, the SMS you got after collection, a photo of the slip or SMS, or your own note written at the time. If you have nothing, you can still add the record as "No evidence" — it will be listed but not counted.

dataPrivacy.a: Your records are saved on your phone and backed up without your ration card number. Aadhaar numbers are removed from text and blacked out in photos before saving. AI features send data only when you tap them. You can delete everything from Settings.
